bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced an AddressSanitizer stack-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 37 in `xmlSnprintfElementContent` at `valid.c:1279`. The staged 2889-byte witness is an `ISO-8859-1` XML document whose internal `<!ELEMENT chapter (...)>` declaration contains a very long comma-separated content model with five colon-bearing QName leaves. On the vulnerable path, one of those later QName leaves is parsed into an `xmlElementContent` node, split into `prefix` and `name`, linked into the returned content-model tree, and then stored on the DTD element declaration for `chapter`. When the instance document later violates that DTD, `xmlValidateElementContent` takes its warning path, allocates stack buffer `expr[5000]`, and recursively formats the expected model into that buffer. In the `XML_ELEMENT_CONTENT_ELEMENT` branch, `xmlSnprintfElementContent` checks `content->prefix` and `content->name` separately against the same cached pre-append `len`, so it never verifies that the combined `prefix:name` fits. After appending the prefix and `:`, the stale second check still passes and `strcat(buf, content->name)` overruns `expr`. The fix resolves this sample by introducing a single combined `qnameLen` check before either append; the patch's later `size - strlen(buf) <= 2` guard addresses another bug in the same function but is not the observed ASan line here.

source.description: First project-side materialization of the attacker-controlled QName token that later becomes the crashing `xmlElementContent` leaf.
source.value_from: The staged 2889-byte `gt_results/arvo_1972/poc` witness contains five `:` characters inside the internal `<!ELEMENT chapter (...)>` declaration, and they all occur in later comma-separated child terms rather than the declaration's first child. Each such later child name is parsed at this loop site into `elem`. The exact one of the five that reaches the crashing recursive formatter call is not disambiguated further because `run_flags.json` has `runtime_disambiguation: false`.

tainted_value_origin.description: On the QName branch, the separated prefix and local name are stored in the `xmlElementContent` node fields that later flow unchanged to `content->prefix` and `content->name` in `xmlSnprintfElementContent`.

root_cause.description: The formatter validates the prefix and local name separately against the same pre-append `len`, so it never checks the combined `prefix:name` length before appending.
root_cause.note: This sample is grounded in the QName-length bug because the saved ASan crash is exactly `valid.c:1279` in the `content->name` append path. The fixing commit replaces these separate checks with a single `qnameLen` check before either append.

coarse_trace.summary: The harness passes the exact staged 2889-byte `ISO-8859-1` XML witness into `xmlReadMemory`.

While parsing the internal `<!ELEMENT chapter (...)>` declaration, libxml2 materializes a later colon-bearing child token, builds an `xmlElementContent` leaf for it, and links that leaf into the returned content-model tree.
The parser stores the built `xmlElementContent` tree directly on the DTD element declaration for `chapter` as `ret->content`.
When the instance later closes `chapter`, validation fetches the stored content model and calls `xmlValidateElementContent(..., warn = 1, ...)`.
Because the actual children do not match the declared model, the warning path allocates stack buffer `expr[5000]` and asks `xmlSnprintfElementContent` to serialize the expected content model into it.

A recursive formatter call reaches a QName leaf with non-NULL `prefix` and `name`; stale separate size checks miss the combined `prefix:name` length, and `strcat(content->name)` overflows `expr` exactly as reported by ASan.

fine_trace.note: Source. In the loop that parses later comma-separated children of the `chapter` content model, this statement materializes one attacker-controlled child token as `elem`. The overflowing formatter call must ultimately use one of these later tokens because the witness's colon-bearing names all occur after earlier separators, not as the declaration's first child.

The parsed token is split at `:` into QName components. On the crashing path `tmp != NULL`, so `l` becomes the prefix length and `tmp` points at the local-name portion that will later be appended separately.

On the QName branch, the new `xmlElementContent` leaf stores the separated prefix and local name on the allocated node. Those exact fields later reappear as `content->prefix` and `content->name` after the same node is returned to the parser and linked into the declaration tree.

The parser stores the returned later-child leaf pointer in `last`. That makes the QName node from steps 2-3 the pending operand that must be attached into the content-model tree before the declaration is returned.

The parser links the pending later-child leaf into the returned tree. If another separator follows, the new operator node stores the leaf as `op->c1` and is hung off `cur->c2` (parser.c:6429-6434 or 6470-6475); if the leaf is the final pending child, loop exit stores it directly as `cur->c2 = last` (parser.c:6528-6531). With `runtime_disambiguation` disabled, the exact one of these tree-link writes taken by the crashing QName leaf is not narrowed further, but one of them must make that leaf reachable from the parser's returned `ret` tree.

When the parser registers the `chapter` declaration, it preserves the returned `content` tree on the DTD element record instead of copying it. The later validation path therefore sees the same tree whose later-child QName leaf was linked in step 5.

When the instance closes `chapter`, `xmlValidateOneElement` calls `xmlValidateElementContent` with `warn` fixed to `1`. That argument is what later allows a content-model mismatch to allocate and fill the diagnostic `expr` buffer instead of only returning failure.

Inside the callee, the same DTD content tree stored on the element declaration is reloaded into the local `cont` variable. This is the exact `cont` later passed to `xmlSnprintfElementContent`; the caller-local `cont` in `xmlValidateOneElement` is not used by the sink path.

The staged instance does not satisfy the declared `chapter` content model, so the validator takes its warning branch rather than returning success or the special `-3` state. That branch is what builds the vulnerable `expr` string.
The warning path allocates the 5000-byte stack buffer later named by ASan and passes both that destination and the callee-local `cont` content tree into `xmlSnprintfElementContent`.

In the crashing recursive formatter call, `len` captures the current output length after earlier terms from the same content model have already been emitted into `expr`. Both later size checks reuse this cached pre-append length.

Root cause. For a QName leaf with non-NULL `content->prefix`, the function validates the prefix and the local name separately against the same cached `len`. It never checks whether the combined `prefix:name` fits after the prefix append, which is the exact obligation added by the patch's new `qnameLen` logic.

Because the first check in step 12 did not return, the formatter appends the prefix and `:` into `buf`. That consumes real space in `expr`, but the cached `len` used by the later name check is not refreshed.

ASan sink. The second check in step 12 still uses the stale pre-prefix `len`, so this `strcat()` executes after step 13 has already reduced the true remaining capacity. The local name copy, reported by ASan as `WRITE of size 37`, therefore writes past the end of caller buffer `expr[5000]`.

poc.trigger: Feeding the staged 2889-byte `poc` to the vulnerable `libxml2_xml_read_memory_fuzzer` makes libxml2 parse an `ISO-8859-1` XML document whose internal `<!ELEMENT chapter (...)>` declaration contains the same large content model with five colon-bearing QName leaves. When the instance later violates that DTD, `xmlValidateElementContent` formats the expected model into `expr[5000]`, and `xmlSnprintfElementContent` overruns that stack buffer at `valid.c:1279` while appending the local-name half of a QName.

format.name: ISO-8859-1 XML with internal DTD content model
format.contract: Exactly the staged 2889-byte witness shape accepted by `libxml2_xml_read_memory_fuzzer`: an `ISO-8859-1` XML document with an internal `<!ELEMENT chapter (...)>` declaration containing the same long comma-separated content model and the same five colon-bearing QName tokens, followed by instance content that drives `chapter` end-element validation into the warning formatter path. This Stage 02 trace is grounded only for that exact witness shape and is not generalized to other DTD layouts, QName choices, or validation states.
